In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FMR algorithm is the best of the three approaches considered in this paper.
the FMR algorithm is the best choice for a single- or multi-GRB GW search.
the FMR algorithm is optimal for a particular choice of the signal duration and that the ad hoc algorithm is a reasonable choice when the true duration is unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the FMR approach is optimal for the case of a GRB with a long-duration GW signal.
the FMR approach is the optimal statistic for a single GRB search, while the ad hoc statistic is the optimal statistic when multiple GRBs are considered.
the FMR statistic and its ad hoc variant are both reasonable candidates for a multi-GRB analysis, but that the ad hoc approach may be more robust.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a search for an association between GRB triggers and GWs can be formulated as a problem in the theory of sequential hypothesis testing.
the ad hoc statistic is more sensitive and hence should be used in searches for a GRB-GW association.
the FMR statistic, while not formally optimal, is robust to the choice of the prior distribution on GW duration and can be used in conjunction with the new statistic for a joint analysis of the two.
